title: First Principles Thinking
coreMove: Strip inherited assumptions from a problem and rebuild from what is actually true.
sourcePressure: The source contrasts reasoning by analogy with reasoning from first principles, names Socratic questioning and the Five Whys, uses the Lego house example, and anchors practical rebuilding in Elon Musk's battery and SpaceX examples.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says ignore tradition, be disruptive, or start from scratch without constraints.

sourceAnchors.name: The Lego house example
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses disassembling a Lego house to show that taking a thing apart creates new possibility beyond incremental improvement
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A Lego house stops being a house when the bricks come loose, and that is exactly when new designs become possible.

sourceAnchors.name: Elon Musk
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Musk's battery and SpaceX examples as anchors for rethinking cost and design through fundamentals
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Musk's useful move was not optimism; it was asking what the materials and physics cost before accepting the market's price tag.

sourceAnchors.name: Socratic questioning and the Five Whys
sourceAnchors.detail: the source names these as the two main techniques for reaching first principles
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The repeated why is not a child's habit here; it is a shovel.

tryThisNow: ask why five times with no object

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a facilities manager told electric maintenance carts are too expensive
exampleSpecs.stakes: the city may keep buying gas carts because the vendor bundle looks inevitable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew separates battery cells, frame, charger, and service contract costs on the bid sheet before accepting the bundled price
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a yellow maintenance cart parked beside a stack of vendor bids

exampleSpecs.audience: a bakery owner whose boxes crush croissants during delivery
exampleSpecs.stakes: delivery growth stalls if the team only buys thicker versions of the same bad box
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Juliette takes the crushed box apart, lists what the pastry actually needs, and rebuilds the package from steam escape and corner pressure instead of copying the old box
exampleSpecs.firstImage: butter flakes stuck to the inside of a collapsed pastry box

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations analyst copying a competitor's room-per-attendant target
exampleSpecs.stakes: rooms may be marked clean while attendants skip safety checks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars walks one room reset with a timer and breaks the job into physical tasks before accepting the industry benchmark
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cart wheel squeaking outside room 417

exampleSpecs.audience: a student team copying last year's winning robot chassis
exampleSpecs.stakes: the copied design may fail the new terrain requirement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chiara asks what the robot must actually cross, carry, and turn around, then removes three copied parts from the table
exampleSpecs.firstImage: aluminum brackets scattered across a plywood bridge mockup

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic manager trying to reduce missed appointments
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients keep missing visits while the clinic buys reminder software by analogy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hadiya asks five whys on one missed visit and finds the real constraint is shift work and bus timing, not forgetfulness
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an unanswered reminder text beside a bus schedule printout

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer technical director upgrading an old lighting setup
exampleSpecs.stakes: a donated rig may look modern but overload the building's electrical limits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Pavel list electricity, throw distance, heat, and cue needs before deciding which donated lights are useful and which are just familiar theater gear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: dust bright in a stage beam above a coil of old cable

skillTargets: rebuild from physical or economic constraints
use Five Whys or Socratic questioning on a live constraint

tryThisNowSpec: Write one problem as two columns: facts I can verify and assumptions I inherited. Rebuild one option using only the first column.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
